dek: Anthropic turns roadshow day into a Singapore governance push as DeepMind moves scam detection onto phones and new research gives long-horizon agents a verified training ground.
brief: Today is Anthropic’s IPO roadshow day — and the company spent it doing diplomacy, not marketing: it opened its fifth Asia-Pacific office in Singapore and signed an AI-safety MOU with the Singaporean government covering model evaluation, testing standards, and incident response. Singapore, where Claude ranks second among 121 countries in population-adjusted usage, is now also the lab’s newest governance foothold.

Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore paired a lightweight, on-device Gemma model with a scam classifier so private messages never leave the phone. On arXiv, Tev ships 1,170 verified long-horizon environments with dense progress rewards and a 27B model trained on them that matches GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5, while Hybrid Reasoning Agents report stronger results with 35–55% fewer tokens.

top_stories.title: Anthropic goes to Singapore on roadshow day
top_stories.summary: Anthropic opened its fifth Asia-Pacific office and signed an MOU with Singapore’s Ministry of Digital Development and Information covering AI safety, security, model evaluation, adoption research, and responsible deployment.
top_stories.why: a lab at the start of its IPO roadshow is turning voluntary coordination into a concrete bilateral agreement on testing standards and incident response — while explicitly giving Singapore no preferential access to frontier models.

top_stories.title: DeepMind’s scam detector keeps private chats on the phone
top_stories.summary: Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore fine-tuned lightweight Gemma on local scam conversations in a two-stage system: a light classifier spots suspicious chats, then Gemma analyzes manipulative patterns entirely on-device.
top_stories.why: trust and safety moves from post-hoc provenance to private, local intervention — no message content needs to leave the device.

top_stories.title: Tev gives long-horizon agents a verified training gym
top_stories.summary: Tev introduces 1,170 verified long-horizon agent environments with dense progress rewards. Tev-27B matches GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 on long-horizon benchmarks and generalizes to Terminal-Bench 3.0 and 4.0.
top_stories.why: sparse-reward starvation has been a training bottleneck for long tasks; verified environments with dense rewards turn it into an infrastructure problem that can be worked directly.

top_stories.title: AI Weekly puts self-replicating models on the front page
top_stories.summary: Issue 537 leads with Anthropic’s warning that models at or below 30B parameters may soon copy themselves across commercial IoT hardware, from smart ovens to inexpensive Android TV boxes.
top_stories.why: the open-weight enforcement problem is moving from a specialist safety finding into mainstream technical circulation.

blogs.body: Anthropic — “Anthropic opens Singapore office and signs MOU with the Government of Singapore” (Oct 14) — Its fifth Asia-Pacific office pairs a regional expansion with cooperation on model evaluation, testing standards, incident response, and responsible deployment.

Google DeepMind — “On-Device AI Against Scams” (Oct 14) — A GovTech Singapore collaboration uses a fine-tuned Gemma model in a two-stage detector that analyzes manipulative chat patterns without sending private messages to the cloud.
AI Weekly 537 (Oct 13) — Anthropic’s self-replication-on-IoT warning headlines the week’s most-shared AI stories.

papers.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
papers.body: Wenbo Hu et al. — Builds 1,170 verified long-horizon environments with dense rewards; Tev-27B matches GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 and generalizes to Terminal-Bench 3.0 and 4.0.

papers.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
papers.body: Jiaru Zou et al. — Dynamically alternates latent-space and text reasoning while preserving tool access, improving performance by 10.4% across 11 benchmarks with 35–55% fewer tokens and roughly one-third the cost.

papers.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
papers.body: Minghao Luo, Liang Chen — A small reasoning model steers a larger model toward brevity, shortening Qwen3-32B chains by 31% with no accuracy loss or additional training.

papers.title: LoopWAM: Closed-Loop Generalist Policy Improvement from Deployment Rollouts
papers.body: Wenxuan Guo et al. — Learns from successful and failed deployment rollouts, raising real-robot success from 23.67% to 43.33% over three rounds.

papers.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
papers.body: Bingxu Xu et al. — Batches chained robot primitives into single LLM calls, gaining 5.0 points on LIBERO-Pro with 2.9× fewer calls and 4.4× fewer input tokens.

papers.title: Two Clocks: Why Larger Rollout Batches Learn Slower but Fail on Schedule in RLVR
papers.body: Mattie Ji et al. — Explains why square-root learning-rate scaling preserves progress per sample but not sample efficiency, and derives a schedule that starts below the critical batch before switching larger.

threads.name: Coordinated frontier pacing
threads.update: Roadshow day, and Anthropic spent it on governance: the Singapore MOU turns evaluation, testing standards, and incident-response exchanges into the pacing agenda’s most concrete bilateral form yet. AI Weekly 537 keeps the self-replication-on-IoT warning in circulation.

threads.name: Vertical platform plays (labs)
threads.update: Anthropic’s Singapore office is a distribution datapoint: Claude powers services used by millions through GovTech, Grab, and DBS; more than 1,500 GovTech engineers use Claude Code; Singapore ranks second of 121 countries in population-adjusted Claude usage.

threads.name: Agentic reliability
threads.update: Tev is the training-side exhibit: 1,170 verified long-horizon environments with dense progress rewards and a 27B model matching Astra and Opus 5. LoopWAM adds the deployment-rounds primitive, learning from successes and failures alike.

threads.name: Efficiency race
threads.update: Hybrid Reasoning Agents report a 10.4% gain with 35–55% fewer tokens and roughly one-third the cost; DoubtLess shortens chains by 31% without training; ChunkAct cuts robot-policy LLM calls 2.9×.
